claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Spark plasma sintering with optimized parameters will reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Spark plasma sintering will preserve the room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Spark plasma sintering produces grain refinement in HfMoTaTiZr.
Spark plasma sintering reduces pores in HfMoTaTiZr.
Densification and grain refinement can reduce the measured density while maintaining mechanical properties.
The spark-plasma-sintered material will have a density below 10.21 g cm−3.
The spark-plasma-sintered material will have a room-temperature yield strength above 1600 MPa.
The spark-plasma-sintered material will have an elevated-temperature yield strength above 855 MPa.
Spark plasma sintering will improve the fracture toughness of HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The proposed testing range extends from room temperature to 1600 °C.

contradictions.description: Pore reduction and densification ordinarily increase bulk/apparent density toward the theoretical density, whereas the predicted outcome requires density to decrease below the as-cast value. No distinction between theoretical, apparent, and relative density is supplied to resolve this inconsistency.

The prediction requires strengths strictly above 1600 MPa and 855 MPa, but the rejection rule only rejects strengths below those values. Results exactly equal to either baseline would fail the stated prediction without falsifying it.
